execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in compromised Warner Music Group online store pages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into form submission events, collects all form data (including payment and personal information), and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, enabling theft of customer data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and sending data to an external, non-legitimate domain is a classic sign of a web skimmer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce JavaScript should not exfiltrate sensitive form data to unknown third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processors may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Sends form data to an external, non-store domain
Obfuscated or injected JavaScript not present in original site code

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the Warner Music Group online store and injects malicious JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in customer browsers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript hooks into form submissions and collects sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of customer data to attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated data is received and stored by the attacker for further exploitation or sale.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of personal and financial information.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into form submission events
Outbound network requests to untrusted or unknown domains upon form submission
Presence of obfuscated or injected scripts not matching site source
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> tags or external JavaScript references in e-commerce checkout pages
Modified or newly added JavaScript files in web server directories
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate e-commerce platform
Frequent small POST requests from client browsers during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce sites for unauthorized JavaScript changes, especially scripts that intercept form submissions and send data to unknown domains. Use web application firewalls to detect and block suspicious outbound requests. Regularly audit site source code and network traffic for signs of skimming activity.
